size_pct_nav: About half of eventual ~$47 million aggregate cost invested in 1976; 1977 table: $19.417 million preferred plus $4.116 million common

drivers.driver: The fundamental direct-distribution business advantage remained intact beneath the financial and operating troubles.
drivers.quote: The fundamental business advantage that GEICO had enjoyed — an advantage that previously had produced staggering success — was still intact within the company, although submerged in a sea of financial and operating troubles.

drivers.driver: The exceptional manager and exceptional franchise made this a rare turnaround worth attempting.
drivers.quote: There aren't many Jack Byrnes in the managerial world, or GEICOs in the business world.

drivers.driver: Minority securities offered earning power far below the cost of acquiring equivalent controlled operations.

entry_valuation_stated: Distressed price; original cutoff preferred terms and exact trade prices unrecovered.
outcome_note: Franchise recovered; Berkshire ultimately acquired the remaining shares. Do not infer that capital support or a return to profitability was certain in July.
sources: Reconstructed from GEICO operating history and 1975 accounts; Jack Byrne Insurance Hall of Fame biography, https://www.insurancehalloffame.org/jack-byrne-simple (pre-cutoff events only)
